title: [review] EDHOC CID decode maps negative ints two's-complement, contradicting RFC 9528 3.3.2 encode side (roundtrip break)
description: P2, found during gt6u fix. ENCODE now per RFC 9528 3.3.2: byte h'21' transports as int -2 (wire 0x21). But DECODE maps wire int 0x20-0x37 two's-complement: wire 0x21 decodes to h'FE' (255-2), not h'21'. Per RFC 3.3.3 (0xFF -> 0x41FF) and 3.3.2, wire int -2 must mean byte string h'21' - so encode(h'21')=0x21 but decode(0x21)=h'FE': roundtrip breaks and cross-endpoint handshakes diverge whenever a CID byte is in 0x20-0x37. Unobservable today (all current CIDs <= 0x17 or multi-byte) but latent interop break. Fix: Python _validate_connection_id int branch (n<0 -> byte 0x1F-n... verify: -1 -> 0x20 => byte 0x20, -24 -> 0x37) and Rust external-crate parse_identifier 0x20-0x37 branch (cbor.rs:110); also responder.rs:263-275 inline msg1 C_I parse rejects negative-int and 0x58+ bstr forms. Add roundtrip tests: bytes 0x00..0xFF encode->decode identity for 1-byte CIDs.
notes: Unblocked by Mark. Fix decode formula, add 0x00..0xFF roundtrip test. Agent-implementable.
